model.name: Styles to Variables Converter
model.description:
This plugin takes your color styles and converts them into new Figma variables, reflecting their structure, names and descriptions.


Local library

If you use your library locally only (in the same file), after running the plugin, you can safely delete all converted styles – layers that were using these styles will now have a variable bound to them.


Published library

In order to safely remove styles using published library, you should do it in 5 steps:

  1. Use plugin (it will preserve styles but with references to the newly created variables).
  2. Publish the library (with styles that now refer to variables instead of hex values).
  3. Update files with new styles (the styles will still be applied to layers, but now with bound variables; depending on the design operations, you may need to wait a few weeks until every current file is updated).
  4. Remove styles from the library.
  5. Publish library (for unknown reasons, I found this step unnecessary, but I would still recommend doing it).


How it works:

  1. Getting all local styles that are convertible (single, solid fills)
  2. Creating new variables based on gotten styles
  3. Binding variables back to styles definition


Keep in mind, that not every "color" style could be converted to variable. Styles with multiple fills, gradients, images, and videos won't be converted, so don't delete them after conversion.


Watch out for duplicate style names because while styles can have duplicate names, variables are still required to have unique names – the plugin skips such duplicates.


Since variables cannot use some characters (., $, {, }) in their name, they are replaced with underscores (_). In some cases it might result in additional duplicates that will be skipped.


Hopefully, this plugin will save you some time. I would greatly appreciate your feedback.

PLUGIN CRAFTED FOR REFOKUS


Plugin Documentation

This plugin extracts font-related properties from your local text styles and converts them into reusable variables. It automatically applies the following variables:

•Font size

•Font weight

•Font family


Additionally, the plugin documents—but does not apply—the following properties:

•Line height

•Letter spacing


This is due to a current Figma limitation: dynamic variables for these properties are not yet supported. As a workaround, these values are stored as string variables for documentation purposes only.


For example:

If the original line-height is 100%, the plugin will store it as a variable with:

variableName: 100%, variableValue: 1em (calculated as 100 ÷ 100 × 1em)


Naming Convention for text styles:


To ensure accurate detection and conversion, your text styles should follow this naming structure:

•Use the prefix title- followed by a number (e.g., title-1) for headings

•Use the prefix text- followed by a number (e.g., text-2) for paragraphs


You can also use suffixes to describe combo classes. For instance:

•text-2-buttonLabel


This will still be recognized as a text-2 style with additional contextual information.

Phase A builds the token system: Paint Styles become Primitive variables, Semantic tokens alias the primitives for light mode, dark mode is generated via shade-mirror alias chains (not hardcoded hex values), and Component tokens add a reference layer on top. Limitations: works on color tokens only. Typography, spacing, and radius tokens are not included in this version.


How to use:

1. Open the plugin and click Scan File

2. Review the scan results, then click Run Full Migration to build variables (Phase A)

3. Review your new Variables in the Variables panel, then click Start Rebinding to reassign all nodes (Phase B)

model.description:
Varlint finds the values in your file that should be variables and are not, tells you which variable each one should be, and binds them.


YOUR IT REVIEW CAN CHECK THIS, NOT TAKE MY WORD

Varlint declares no network access, and Figma prints that on this page beside the last-updated date — so the person who approves plugins where you work can confirm it without contacting me. Your variables and your layers are already in your file; nothing about them leaves your machine, there is nothing to sign in to, and no usage is measured. There is nothing to fill in on a security questionnaire, and no service that can go down and take the plugin with it.


ALL 46 PLACES

Figma allows a variable in forty-six different places: sizes, spacing, corners, stroke weights, fill and stroke colour, every text property, effects, layout grids and component properties. Varlint looks at all of them. That number is not typed in by hand — a test reads Figma's own type definitions and fails if the two ever disagree.


IT SAYS WHICH VARIABLE

Finding a raw value is the easy half. If a variable in your file already holds that value, Varlint names it. If none does, it says so. It never offers to invent variables for you — your token set is yours.


DECISIONS, NOT ROWS

"Every padding of 16 should be spacing/md" is one decision that happens to touch thousands of layers. Varlint shows it as one row with the count on it, so a file's worth of work is a list you can actually read before you agree to it.


IT FOLLOWS YOUR FILE, NOT A RULEBOOK

Varlint reads how far your file has already got in each group — colour, spacing, corners, text — and only ticks the ones you are visibly already doing. A file that has never bound a width is not asked to start. When several variables hold the same value, the one your file already binds there wins. Nothing is guessed from variable names.


WHEN IT CAN'T, IT SAYS SO

Every binding is read back after it is written, and anything that did not take is listed with the reason: the layer is gone, the variable is gone, Figma will not allow it there. A binder that fails quietly is worse than one that fails.


FREE AND PAID

model.name: Apply variables
model.description:
Already have your variables set up and want to bulk apply them to your work? You can swap styles with variables or apply variables that match raw number values to elements in any file with access to your variables collections! 


Watch a demo video of the plug-in in action here.


Swap with variables by name

  1. Example: elements with color style background/default applied to them will have the variable called background/default applied to them after the plug-in works its magic. 
  2. Reads names from applied color styles or applied variables and lets you swap that with a variable of a given collection with the same name
  3. Currently available for color variables.


Apply matching variables (autofix) to radius or AutoLayout dimension properties

  1. Example: you have a variable called container-radius/default with a value of 8. After the plugin runs, all containers with 8 as their corner radius would have the container-radius/default variable applied. 
  2. Currently available for number variables (corner radius, item spacing, padding and row gap).
  3. If there are several variables with the same value, it chooses the first variable with the same scope settings as the property would need. If no variable matches the scope, it picks the first one that has generic scope that matches.
  4. We rank variables by name, meaning a variable with padding in its name will be preferred for the auto layout properties. One with gap or spacing in its name will be preferred for the gap properties. One with radii, cornerRadius or radius will be preferred for the radius properties


Learn more about variable scoping from the Figma docs here


How to use

1. Ensure you have access to variables in your local file or through a published team library. 

2. Select the elements on the canvas that you want to apply your variables

3. Run the plugin and choose which kind of variable you want to apply: Swap with variables by name or Apply matching variables (autofix)

5. Select the name of the collection that has the variables you want to apply 

6. Choose where you want the variables to be applied 

  1. Selection (optimal performance) - If you’ve selected specific elements on the Figma canvas to apply variables 
  2. Page - scans all elements on the current page and apply variables 
  3. Document - scans all elements on every page within the Figma File and applies variables (can be slow)

model.name: Style Quick Actions
model.description:
Style Quick Actions - Figma Plugin

Quick actions for applying styles to selected including Text, Fill, Stroke, Effect, and Grid. Works with local styles and published Team Library styles. Also works with Color Variables.


Local styles will always be available options, no management necessary. To learn how to access styles from other files, read 'Using Published Figma Team Library Styles' below.


Recommended Use


Quick Key Combos

To quickly select the commands from the quick actions input, type:

  1. qfl for Fill
  2. qsk for Stroke
  3. qtx for Text
  4. qgd for Grid
  5. qef for Effect


For example, to set a Fill quickly, type: ⌘/ > qfl > pri-blu-1 to match 'primary-blue-fill-01'


Key Bindings

You can set custom keybindings on MacOS that will automatically open one of the style fills. This is probably possible on Windows too, but I don't know the details.

  1. Navigate to: System Preferences > Keyboard > Shortcuts > App Shortcuts > click "+"
  2. Select Application: "Figma.app" and set shortcut for plugin commands by pasting in the "Menu Title" in this format: Plugins->Plugin Name->Plugin Command


I prefer to set the actions for setting Fill, Stroke, and Text to:

  1. ⌃F - Fill - Plugins->Style Quick Actions->Fill
  2. ⌃S - Stroke - Plugins->Style Quick Actions->Stroke
  3. ⌃T - Text - Plugins->Style Quick Actions->Text


Read more on Apple Support


Using Published Figma Team Library Styles


To use Team Library Styles in another file

  1. Publish your file as a Figma 'Team Library'
  2. Publish your file by running 'Style Quick Actions > Publish Library Styles'
  3. In the another file, run 'Style Quick Actions > Toggle Library Styles' and select the library
  4. The Styles will now be available in the Fill, Stroke, Text, Effect, and Grid Style selectors


You will have to update Published Styles every time the Team Library Styles are updated.

  1. Update Published Styles by running 'Style Quick Actions > Publish Library Styles' again.


Delete styles by running 'Style Quick Actions > Remove Library Styles'


Caveats:

  1. Library Styles are saved in this plugin based on their source file name. If that file name changes, the plugin will treat it as a new Published Library Style. If you change the a source file name, delete the old one and re-publish.
  2. There is a max memory limit of 1MB for each plugin. This means there is a limited number of styles you can publish via this plugin. There is a percentage % next to the Published Style name that displays how much of the total memory each Library takes up.
  3. You can't Toggle Published Styles in their own source library. Those styles are always available locally.
